scope: Proposition 3.5 (Index rigidity) of the manuscript “The Solomon–Yau least-volume theorem” (preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 349 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b44def9b041e8f31), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every smooth, closed, connected, embedded minimal hyper- surface Σm ⊂ Sm+1, m ≥ 2, which is not totally geodesic has ind(Σ) ≥ m + 3. If ind(Σ) = m + 3, then, up to an ambient isometry, its image is Sk ⎛ ⎝ √ k m ⎞ ⎠ × Sm−k ⎛ ⎝ √ m − k m ⎞ ⎠ for some 1 ≤ k < m. In particular, such a hypersurface of volume less than am has index strictly greater than m + 3.
